text:
Sana (infra): quick flag  eu-west3 pool-12 showing persistent p99 jitter since 07:05UTC. Not standard NIC saturation pattern.
Marcus (sre): saw it. p50 fine, but p99 jumps ~400ms sporadically. Any noisy-host signals?
ops-bot: [telemetry] pool-12 rack-7 IO write latency +280% since 07:03 (link: https://telemetry.redwood/egress/1765012345).
Sana (infra): digging. Correlation looks like a tenant (tenant:greenbeam) running large embedding sweeps that spawn many concurrent NVMe streams. It's causing host-level IO contention and slab churn.
Ivy (platform): moving dedicated slices is painful for SLAs. We could provision a fractional carveout: reserve ~1-2 GPUs per rack as "quiet slots" and route background batch prefixes there. That avoids evicting paid slices.
Ralph (sales-eng): greenbeam has reserved capacity for prod; they will be unhappy with evictions. Fractional carveout sounds promising but what's the cost hit?
Sana (infra): preliminary calc: carving 2 GPUs per affected rack -> capacity loss ~3.8% in eu-west3 pool-12. If we period-limit it we can limit cost to a few hours.
Marcus (sre): operationally we need an automated short-lived carveout workflow: 1) annotate racks affected, 2) set routing rule for `batch/emb-*` prefixes -> carveout-pool, 3) set QoS max-egress=150mbps on carveout to avoid egress spikes.
Ivy (platform): agree. We have a feature `fractional-reserve` in routerctl but it's behind flag; can run gated rollout. Command draft (dry-run):
```
routerctl reserve add --pool=pool-12 --racks=rack-7,rack-8 --gpus=2 --name=quiet-carve-1765012345 --ttl=4h --dry-run
routerctl prefix add --tenant=greenbeam --prefix=batch/emb --target=quiet-carve-1765012345 --force --dry-run
qosctl set --tenant=greenbeam --tag=carveout-softcap --max-egress=150mbps --ttl=30m --dry-run
```
Marcus (sre): prefer staging canary: apply to one rack first, measure p99 and KV-miss rate for 10m. Roll forward if stable.
Sana (infra): timeline: 07:20 - reserve carveout on rack-7 (dry-run now), 07:30 - canary prefix shift weight=0.25, 07:40 - evaluate, 07:45 - ramp to full carveout weight=1.0 for batch prefixes, 10:00 - release carveout.
Ralph (sales-eng): please cc `notify:sales-eng` so I can update the account team and TAM. We'll craft a gentle note to greenbeam saying background batch jobs may be routed to quieter slots during maintenance window.
ops-bot: [alloc] current preemptible-warm headroom in eu-west3 ~22%; dedicated headroom ~8%. Carveout will reduce available dedicated by ~3.8%.
Ivy (platform): note: embeddings on preemptible-warm thrash KV cache. That's why carveout is better than moving to preemptible-warm. Carveout slots should be isolated cache-wise (separate kvcache partition) if possible.
Marcus (sre): add `kvcache:isolate=true` annotation when reserving. Also add `qos=frac-reserve` tag so autoscaler doesn't backfill with noisy jobs.
Sana (infra): running dry-run reserve now. If dry-run passes I'll push actual reserve and prefix rule at 07:20.
Marcus (sre): also add alert: p99 > baseline +200ms OR KV-eviction-rate > 2x -> auto rollback changes and notify infra-oncall.
Sana (infra): agreed. infra-oncall will own rollback. Who's oncall?
Marcus (sre): I'll be oncall at that time. I'll shadow infra-oncall for rollback ops.
Ralph (sales-eng): greenbeam replied in thread: "we can reduce parallelism for non-prod sweeps by 50% if needed. Thanks for the heads up."
Ivy (platform): follow-up: I'll open PLAT ticket to make fractional-reserve self-serve in console and track per-pool egress headroom (PLAT-9310).
Sana (infra): notes for post-run: collect eviction logs, kvcache-hit-rate, per-tenant retransmit count, and cost delta estimate.
ops-bot: [action] reserve dry-run created by Sana at 2025-08-12T07:18:12Z (id: r-dry-1765012345).
Sana (infra): applying reserve now. Will update with canary metrics in ~15m. Keep this channel for anomalies only.
Marcus (sre): canary flip in 2m. Watching p50/p95/p99, KV-miss, and NVMe write latency.
Ivy (platform): reminder: if carveout reduces available dedicated below threshold for other critical tenants we have an automatic fallback to route lower-priority slices to preemptible-cold.
Sana (infra): :thumbsup: all set. Thanks team.
